humanize_6c.tool: Undetectable.ai Humanizer (humanize.undetectable.ai, model v11, 'More Human') via seo-tools/humanize.mjs
humanize_6c.applied_to: ALL flowing prose: intro (3 paragraphs), 5 FAQ answers, author note, and the 6 feature-card descriptions. NOT applied to: H1, meta title/description, section headings, feature TITLES, FAQ questions, comparison rows, pricing keyword line, schema — these are kept verbatim to protect keyword placement + structure.

per_piece_AI_before_after.note: Humanizer output was lightly proofread (fixed grammar slips, first-person 'I'->'we', a factual 'yellow pins', and re-inserted the 2 in-text links in intro). f1/f3 were hand-cleaned where the humanizer garbled them.

prose_extract.note: The run book's 'extract page prose to detect/<slug>.txt' check. PASSES after humanizing.

full_main.note: Full <main> includes structured UI (card titles, comparison cells, stat labels, breadcrumbs) the detector scores holistically as AI regardless of prose. Humanizing all 6 feature descriptions to ~0 moved full-main only 66.9->66.1, confirming the structured components — not the prose — drive the full-main score. Not meaningfully reducible without gutting the page's conversion structure.

plagiarism_winston.verdict: PASS — original after humanizing (humanizer rephrasing did not introduce matches).

keyword_retention_check._new_step: Added per operator concern that humanizing could drop owned keywords.
keyword_retention_check.note: On first humanized build, the 4 secondary keywords were ABSENT (they were not verbatim on the page even pre-humanize). Backfilled naturally via a pricing-section sentence (a non-humanized, keyword-stable field). All owned keywords now present. Primary keyword also remains in H1/title/schema (never humanized).

_done_check: Gate 3 satisfied: Winston plagiarism 0% (binding); prose AI-detection HUMAN (47.5) after the 6c humanize step. Full-main score documented as structurally driven. Keyword retention verified + backfilled.
